effects: Emits one ExitRequest(msg.sender, pubkey) event for each validator public key passed; nothing else happens on chain.
No tokens or ETH move, no approval is set, no state is written. The function is not payable.

Off chain, Kiln reads the event and may exit the listed validators. Their stake then stops earning rewards and goes back to the validators' withdrawal credentials, which are set at deposit and are not in this call.
formats.shown: "Request Validator Exit", then every validator public key you are asking to exit, shown as raw hex.

findings.title: requestExit only emits a signal; the off-chain exit and where the withdrawn ETH goes cannot be shown.
findings.evidence: ExitRequestContract.sol requestExit: `emit ExitRequest(msg.sender, validators_[i]);` is the only statement. The calldata has no recipient or amount. The case 0 reader was unsure where the funds go and how much comes back.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show this. If wanted, a short note in the intent or label could say the exit is processed by Kiln off-chain, e.g. "Request Kiln to exit validators".

cases.notes: The mined tx has no token, ETH or approval effects. It only emitted the event. The screen lists the single validator pubkey that was in the calldata. The reader correctly understood it as an exit request for one validator.
